function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity wasn’t “discovered” by a single individual—it emerged from centuries of observations and experiments. Early Greek philosophers like Thales noted static electricity, while later scientists such as William Gilbert (1600s) coined the term *electricus*. In the 18th century, Luigi Galvani’s work on bioelectricity and Alessandro Volta’s invention of the voltaic pile laid foundations for modern electrical science. By the 19th century, Michael Faraday’s discoveries of electromagnetic induction and James Clerk Maxwell’s equations unified electricity and magnetism into a single theory. Thus, the understanding of electricity evolved through contributions from many thinkers rather than a single discoverer.
